title: What kind of collection is it?
lede: Two questions name it. Four more words add to the name.

values.label: An entry changes after it is written

cells.gloss: kept current, one entry per thing
an event's record, rewritten until the event ends
a thing's record, never edited once written
one entry per happening, added over time, never edited; also called a log or a ledger

grid.note: A snapshot is one stream entry: a registry as it stood at one time (docs/registries.md). For a collection rebuilt from other files, ask what each entry records, not how the file is rebuilt.

add.gloss: rebuilt from other files, with nothing checking it against them
each entry carries a status, such as open or done

renames.why: Both are rebuilt in place from other files and may lag them; a snapshot is a dated reading kept as written.
A session record is rewritten while the session runs, so it is not a stream.
lib/gh-boot.js adds each request with status 0 and fills it in when the request settles, so its entries change after they are written.
It holds several collections and is not one.

open.question: Collections of material, whose entries are text kept to be used rather than records of a thing or an event (lists/jot.json, chron/dump/, shortcuts/incoming/, home's chron/ log), fit neither column. Leave them off the grid?
open.why: Say so where the grid is stated. A third column would add two more empty boxes, and inbox already names the material collections that drain. Home's chron/ log is the one that stays and is edited in place, so calling it a log puts it nowhere on the grid.

open.question: What should the empty box at top right, an event's record that changes while the event is live, be called?
open.why: Call each one by what it holds, and stop calling these streams or ledgers. No reader proposed a word, and the two members, session records and the request record in window.__traffic, are already named by what they hold.

open.question: Request files that close when a result file is added beside them (errands, proposals) sit in the empty box at lower left. Call them a request queue?
open.why: It is a standard term and collides with nothing in the estate's vocabulary. One reader proposed it, another found the same gap, and all three poster readers sent errands to this call.

open.question: Should a collection that drops its oldest entries past a cap, such as window.__traffic or state/sessions.json, get its own word, window?
open.why: A cap says how long entries are kept, so state it where the collection is described. Each capped collection already sits in a box by its entries; the cap changes how long they stay, not what they are.

by: Placed by one reader's hand coding of 33 collections across web-tools, home and web-tools-private. Four readers, working blind to one another, named the same two questions and the same four add-on words. Where the coding and docs/registries.md disagreed, the poster follows docs/registries.md.
